list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: Tetranuclear ytterbium iodide disulfido sulfido cluster

material_class.structural_family: Square Yb4 disulfido cluster with a μ4-sulfido cap

properties.summary: The sharp visible absorption bands are assigned to disulfido-to-Yb(III) and sulfido-to-Yb(III) charge-transfer excitations.

source_locations.location: Main text, lines 11–17 and Figure 1; lattice THF from supplied CCDC catalog formula
Supplied structures-catalog row for this DOI

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Four seven-coordinate Yb(III) ions form a square. Four μ-η²:η²-disulfido ligands bridge adjacent ions, and one μ4-sulfido ligand caps the Yb4 plane. Two iodides bind opposite Yb ions on the same side of the plane; THF ligands complete the coordination spheres.

synthesis.procedure: The preferred route reacts either “YbI(SPh)” or “YbI(SPh)2” with 2.25 equivalents of elemental sulfur per Yb in THF at room temperature. An initial route oxidized YbI with 1 equivalent of elemental sulfur; the red product was separated from precipitated YbI3(THF)x by fractional crystallization.

reagents.amount: 1 equivalent of either precursor per 2.25 equivalents of S
reagents.name: Ytterbium iodide thiophenolate precursor
reagents.role: Alternative ytterbium starting materials in the preferred route

reagents.name: Elemental sulfur
reagents.role: Sulfur source in the preferred route

reagents.name: Ytterbium monoiodide
reagents.role: Starting material in the initial route

synthesis.temperature: Room temperature for the preferred route
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: The initial route yielded a red product by fractional crystallization, but separation from the major YbI3-containing product was problematic.
synthesis.yield: 40% isolated yield by the preferred route

properties.summary: The crystalline thulium analogue is reported to have an unusually sharp visible spectrum; the 404 and 460 nm absorption bands observed for compound 1 are absent.

synthesis.procedure: Parallel experiments with thulium gave the crystalline analogue; the main text does not provide its specific starting materials, quantities, or preparation procedure.
